Subject: [Clearwave] Post-cutover: traffic >1400B failing to egress

Markus / Laura —

We completed the private-connectivity cutover at 02:00 PDT to the new transit appliance. Since then we're seeing intermittent application errors for large payloads (file uploads and TLS responses) sourced from our on-prem app tier. Small requests (<=1400 bytes) go through fine. 

Symptoms:
- TCP sessions establish, but large transfers stall around 1460-1500 bytes and then time out after retries.
- Packet captures attached show MSS/PMTU blackhole behavior on egress path.
- Visible only from our staging region (staging-us-west), prod not impacted yet.

Attached: capture_flow_small_and_large.pcapng (two flows: small vs large)

Can you confirm whether there were any MTU or PMTU clamps applied on transit, or route changes that might steer large flows to a different egress path? Appreciate urgent eyes — client is seeing degraded uploads.

— Erin (ops-staging@clearwave.com)
Ops — Clearwave Health

Erin / team — quick outputs from the staging slice:

Traceroutes (selected):
- ICMP: 10.10.42.11 -> 44.55.66.77 hops: transit1 (10.248.1.1) -> cloud-edge-a (198.51.100.5) -> peer-gw (203.0.113.10) -> destination
- TCP (sport 443): same hop count but at cloud-edge-a we see TTL decrements + MTU=1420 observed in probe responses.

Interface counters on our VPC peering appliance (cloud-edge-a):
- egress-mtu-errors: sporadic drops correlated with timestamps Erin sent
- no ACL denies logged for those flows

I pulled security group logs — no denies. However, I do see asymmetric egress selection for large flows: route hash is flipping to a second egress path for packets with DF flag set. That suggests a path MTU difference between the two egress hops.

Next steps I'm running:
- confirm MSS clamp policy on our egress NAT and peer-gw (cc netops)
- copy of tcpdump conditioned on DF flag and large MSS
- schedule 15-min outage window proposal if we need to shift traffic to the consistent path while we fix MTU.

Laura Bennett

Subject: Re: [Clearwave] Post-cutover: traffic >1400B failing to egress

Quick findings from conntrack / NAT appliances: attached dump (conntrack-dump-0819.txt). Observations:
- Conntrack table shows many transient entries for the affected 10.10.42.0/24 hosts; sessions are present but we see repeated retransmit state (SYN/ACK retrans).
- No evidence of NAT port exhaustion; table growth is normal but we see a cluster of flows with 0 MSS option or where MSS is not negotiated (likely because DF fragments are being dropped).
- MSS clamp configuration on the private NAT was unchanged in the cutover deploy; I checked the config history and there was no deliberate MSS policy push.

Action I'm taking now:
- Temporarily apply an MSS clamp to 1360 on the staging NAT to mitigate while we isolate the upstream path mismatch. This will prevent fragmentation at the cost of slightly lower MTU.
- Coordinate with netops to identify which upstream hop advertises a lower MTU and why traffic is being hashed to it for DF-set flows.

I'll post results within 30 minutes after the clamp goes in.

— Karthik

Subject: Re: [Clearwave] Post-cutover: traffic >1400B failing to egress

Summary & plan (post triage):

What happened:
- Cutover introduced a second egress next-hop that advertises a 1420 MTU. Traffic hashing rules routed DF-set/large-payload flows sporadically to that hop, while other packets took the higher-MTU path. The mismatch produced effective PMTU blackholing for large transfers.

Immediate mitigation performed:
- Karthik applied an MSS clamp of 1360 on the staging NAT appliance at 12:25 PDT. Post-clamp the failing flows resumed normally in the captures; attached conntrack dump shows sessions stable.
- We temporarily pinned staging routing to the higher-MTU egress for flows with destination X.X.X.X to prevent path flipping.

Permanent remediation items:
1) Netops will normalize MTU across both egress next-hops (open ticket NET-4921) — owner: netops@cloudpartner.com.
2) We will add an egress-path sticky-hash rule for DF-set flows until MTU parity is confirmed.
3) Add an automated PMTU monitor in the Redwood Console to detect new mismatches during cutovers.
4) Update runbook: include conntrack and DF-flag conditioned captures as first-step in cutover checklist.

Drive doc & ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/NET-4921 | https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2bC_sample_flowmap

Erin — thanks for flagging. Can you confirm whether you want us to run a validation sweep across prod tomorrow morning (low traffic window)? If yes we'll schedule and coordinate the maintenance window with you.

— Markus

Redwood Inference
